issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath §6.2 Comparison (decimal sub-second semantics) + dual-engine lockstep invariant
issues.evidence: SELECT fhirpath(...,'@2018-03-01T10:30:00.1234 < @2018-03-01T10:30:00.1236'): native=false, python=true; equality native=true, python=false; same for @T times and > with .1234 vs .1230. Root cause: extensions/fhirpath/src/fhirpath/evaluator.cpp parseDateTimeParts/parseTimeParts truncate fractional seconds to 3 digits (ms_str.substr(0,3)) and compareDateTimes compares the truncated int; Python fallback uses full-precision timestamp(). Repro: .temp/qa/fp14_historian_2026_08_18/probe.py
issues.root_cause: Native parseDateTimeParts/parseTimeParts truncated fractional seconds to 3 digits; compareDateTimes compared the truncated millisecond int, losing sub-millisecond precision vs the Python fallback's full-precision timestamp().
issues.resolution: Added untruncated frac_digits to DateTimeParts in evaluator.cpp (both parsers); compareDateTimes now compares whole seconds via the field loop and sub-second fraction digits as decimals (right-padded to equal width) per §6.2 decimal comparison semantics. Extension rebuilt and redeployed to repo bundle + user site-packages. 19-case dual-engine parity regression test added.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath §6.2 (types differ -> error -> empty); conversion table defines no Time<->Date/DateTime conversion
issues.evidence: DateTimeComparisons.greater_than(FHIRTime('T12:00:00'), FHIRDateTime('2018-03-01T12:00')) -> False; also Time vs Date -> False. Engine expression @T12:00:00 < @2014-01-01 -> empty. 10th instance of exported-helper-API-forgotten family.
issues.root_cause: Helper _engine_compare called engine FP_*.compare() directly, bypassing the expression-level type guard; FP_Time.compare accepts any FP_TimeBase (incl. FP_Date/FP_DateTime) and returns a definitive result where no implicit conversion exists.
issues.resolution: Type guard in _engine_compare: Time never compares to Date/DateTime (no implicit conversion) -> None/empty. Unit regression test added.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath §6.2 (invalid/uncertain temporal input -> empty); public helper API must not crash
issues.evidence: FHIRDate.from_string('2018-03-01+05:00') is accepted (dates carry no offset per spec) and DateTimeComparisons.less_than(<that>, FHIRDate('2018-03-02')) raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'compare' — FP_Date(invalid lexical) returns None and _engine_compare calls .compare() unguarded.
issues.root_cause: _engine_compare dereferenced FP temporal constructors that return None for invalid lexical forms; FHIRDate.from_string over-accepts offset-carrying dates.
issues.resolution: None-guard on engine node construction in _engine_compare; invalid lexical operand -> None (empty). Unit regression test added.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath §6.2 partial-date comparison precision walk; implicit Date->DateTime conversion is defined
issues.evidence: @2018-03-02 > @2018-03-01T12:00 -> true in both engines (definitive at shared day precision despite different precision levels). Spec prose conflicts: precision-mismatch -> empty stated unconditionally, but the walk 'proceeding to the finest precision' stops at first difference. No official fixture covers Date-vs-DateTime ordering. Both engines agree; no parity divergence. Filed for human/spec-clarification tracking only.
